title.en: Jon Ossoff blasts ‘draft-dodging, crook president’ in latest war of words with Trump – US politics live
title.zh: 乔恩·奥索夫在与特朗普的最新口水战中抨击其为“逃避兵役的骗子总统”——美国政治直播

summary.en: Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff, campaigning for re-election in Georgia, criticized former President Donald Trump, calling him a "draft-dodging, crook president" and accusing him of recklessly leading the nation into an unresolvable war. Trump responded by posting an image of a map of the Strait of Hormuz.
summary.zh: 正在佐治亚州竞选连任的民主党参议员乔恩·奥索夫批评前总统唐纳德·特朗普，称其为“逃避兵役的骗子总统”，并指责他鲁莽地将国家拖入一场无法结束或获胜的战争。特朗普则发布了一张霍尔木兹海峡的地图。

body.en: The Democratic senator, who is currently running for re-election in Georgia, says Trump ‘has plunged our nation recklessly into a war he knows not how to end or to win’ Sign up for the US Breaking News email President Donald Trump posted an image of a map of the strait of Hormuz on his social media platform Truth Social, with a circle around the strait and the words “New US Territory” as the title on Tuesday morning. This follows comments made on Friday at a speech at a police academy on Long Island, New York, where Trump said “After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I’ll be declaring the Hormuz strait a territory of the United States. … Essentially, that’s what it is. We have the blockade. No ships get through unless we want them to.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 这位目前正在佐治亚州竞选连任的民主党参议员表示，特朗普“鲁莽地让我们的国家陷入了一场他不知道如何结束或获胜的​​战争”。周二上午，唐纳德·特朗普总统在他的社交媒体平台Truth Social上发布了一张霍尔木兹海峡地图的图片，该图片在海峡周围画了一个圆圈，标题是“新美国领土”。此前，特朗普周五在纽约长岛的一所警察学院发表讲话时表示，“在我们击败伊朗之后，伊朗战况非常惨重，我很快就会宣布霍尔木兹海峡是美国的领土……本质上就是这样。我们有封锁。除非我们愿意，否则任何船只都不能通过。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: Political discourse often devolves into sharp accusations and verbal attacks, as seen in this latest exchange. Proverbs reminds us that reckless words can wound deeply, like sword thrusts, creating division rather than understanding. May we seek wisdom to speak words that heal and build up, even amidst disagreement.
reflection.zh: 政治言论常演变为尖锐的指责和言语攻击，如同这则新闻中的最新交锋。箴言提醒我们，鲁莽的言语如同刀剑刺人，只会制造分裂而非理解。愿我们寻求智慧，即使在意见相左时，也能说出医治和造就的话语。

verse.textEn: The words of the reckless pierce like swords, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
verse.textZh: 说话浮躁的，如刀刺人；智慧人的舌头却为医人的良药。

title.en: Tupac Shakur murder trial: former security officer describes witnessing aftermath of shooting – latest updates
title.zh: 图帕克·沙库尔谋杀案审判：医学专家就说唱歌手尸检作证——最新进展

summary.en: A forensic pathologist, Dr. Lisa Gavin, presented evidence from Tupac Shakur’s autopsy report and photos during the ongoing murder trial. The District Court Judge relayed questions from the jury directly to the medical examiner as the court seeks to understand the circumstances of the rapper's death.
summary.zh: 在图帕克·沙库尔谋杀案的审判中，法医病理学家丽莎·加文博士就说唱歌手的尸检报告和照片提供了证据。地区法院法官卡莉·基尔尼直接向法医转达了陪审团的几个问题。

body.en:
Minutes after testifying that it was “impossible” that Reggie Wright Jr was involved in the murder of Tupac Shakur , James McDonald, a former associate of Death Row Records executive Suge Knight, refused to go into detail about the beating of Orlando Anderson at the MGM Hotel, and how that beating fueled ongoing tensions between rival factions in Compton.

“I told every attorney that tried to get me in here, you’d better treat me as a hostile witness. And I think that’s where I’m about to know now, because you’re asking me questions--I can’t answer those questions.”

Right after Shakur’s shooting, McDonald said he immediaely left Las Vegas for California. “We knew we were going to have neighborhood issues,” he said. “It’s time to go and protect your home front. Like the other side was being prepared and was prepared to do things because Orlando got beat up in there ,and that’s something that you don’t tolerate.”

Asked why Orlando was targeted in Las Vegas, McDonald said: “I’m aware of a lot of things, things that was going on. People ain’t talked about it in 30 years. Today ain’t one of them. I don’t mean to be funny. But, here’s the things: a lot of things happened that night, a lot of things happened weeks and weeks after that night. Me or anybody else bringing up the dead is wrong. A lot of people got hurt behind this situation in itself.”

“Living the life in how we lived in Compton is one thing. You bring back all of the guys who made it, like me, I’m 61 years old now, to rehash and relive this situation.”

It’s worth noting that Orlando Anderson, the nephew of Duane “Keefe D" Davis, whose beating prosecutors say prompted Shakur’s killing, has been dead since 1998.
body.zh: 内华达州克拉克县的法医病理学家丽莎·加文博士现在作为专家分析员出庭作证，审查图帕克·沙库尔尸检报告和尸体照片。 实际进行尸检的法医已经去世，凸显了在死亡实际发生 30 年后举行谋杀案审判的挑战。 加文指出，她 1996 年就读于医学院，但在解释证据方面拥有多年经验。

reflection.en: In the pursuit of justice, a trial meticulously examines evidence and testimony to uncover the truth. Proverbs 18:17 reminds us that a thorough examination is crucial, ensuring all perspectives are heard before a judgment is made. This careful process reflects a societal commitment to accountability and the diligent search for facts.
reflection.zh: 在寻求公义的过程中，审判会细致地审查证据和证词，以揭示真相。箴言18:17提醒我们，在做出判断之前，彻底的审查至关重要，确保所有观点都被听取。这一严谨的过程反映了社会对问责制和勤勉寻求事实的承诺。

verse.textZh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理；但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

title.en: Second major fire at south London recycling centre in under three months
title.zh: 三个月内伦敦南部回收中心发生第二起重大火灾

summary.en: Fifteen fire engines tackling blaze at Landmann Way in Deptford involving 50 tonnes of household waste Fifteen fire engines and about 100 firefighters are tackling a blaze in a south-east London recycling plant for the second time this summer. London fire brigade said the blaze...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Fifteen fire engines and about 100 firefighters are tackling a blaze in a south-east London recycling plant for the second time this summer.

London fire brigade said the blaze on Landmann Way in Deptford involves about 50 tonnes of household waste stored at a recycling facility.

The brigade was first called just before 8pm and crews from East Greenwich, Old Kent Road, Deptford and surrounding fire stations went to the scene.

In a video posted online, flames and smoke could be seen billowing above the surrounding buildings near a railway line.

Firefighters tackled a blaze at the same facility in June when a van and a car were destroyed and one man was treated on the scene by the London ambulance service.

Station commander Duncan Rees said: “Approximately 100 firefighters are tackling a large fire at a recycling centre on an industrial estate on the border of Bermondsey and north Lewisham.

“First calls were received at 19.58 and 15 fire appliances are now in attendance. Fire crews along with colleagues from partner blue light services are working hard in difficult conditions to bring the fire under control.

“One of the brigade’s 32-metre turntable ladders and one 64-metre turntable ladder are being used as water towers to tackle the flames from above.”

People have been asked to avoid the area and keep their doors and windows closed where possible because of the large amount of smoke.

Rail services into London Bridge from New Cross are affected because the fire has blocked railway lines, National Rail said.
body.zh: 今年夏天，15 辆消防车和约 100 名消防员正在第二次扑灭伦敦东南部回收工厂的火灾。 伦敦消防队表示，德普特福德兰德曼路 (Landmann Way) 起火涉及回收设施中储存的约 50 吨生活垃圾。 晚上 8 点前，该消防队首次接到报警，来自东格林威治、老肯特路、德普特福德和周边消防站的消防人员赶赴现场。 在网上发布的视频中，可以看到火焰和烟雾在铁路线附近的周围建筑物上空翻滚。 六月，消防队员在同一设施内扑灭火灾，一辆面包车和一辆汽车被毁，伦敦救护车在现场救治了一名男子。 消防站指挥官邓肯·里斯 (Duncan Rees) 表示：“大约 100 名消防员正在伯蒙西 (Bermondsey) 和刘易舍姆 (Lewisham) 北部交界处的一个工业区的回收中心扑灭大火。 “19点58分接到第一个电话，目前已有15辆消防车赶到现场。消防人员与蓝光服务合作伙伴的同事在困难的条件下努力控制火势。 “该旅的一个32米转盘梯和一个64米转盘梯被用作水塔，从上方扑灭火焰。” 由于烟雾大量，人们被要求避开该地区，并尽可能关闭门窗。 国家铁路公司表示，由于火灾堵塞了铁路线，从新十字到伦敦桥的铁路服务受到影响。

body.en:
There have been reports of poor conditions on board the USS Abraham Lincoln, which the US Navy says will soon be brought home from the Middle East.

The aircraft carrier was originally expected back in May - but the US war with Iran has kept it at sea for around 250 days straight.

BBC Verify has used satellite imagery to monitor the warship's movements which last docked in December last year.

title.en: Disney and ABC sue Trump's media regulator to stop early licence renewal
title.zh: 迪士尼和美国广播公司起诉特朗普的媒体监管机构，以阻止提前续签牌照

summary.en: Disney and ABC are suing the Trump administration's media regulator to prevent an early license renewal, alleging the administration is retaliating against ABC due to its disapproval of the network's broadcasts.
summary.zh: 迪士尼和美国广播公司（ABC）正在起诉特朗普政府的媒体监管机构，以阻止其提前续签牌照，指控政府因不认可ABC的广播内容而对其进行报复。

body.en:
Disney and ABC have filed a lawsuit to stop the Trump administration from launching an early licence renewal process, arguing that the network is being unfairly targeted over its editorial content.

"Government censorship is deeply un-American," the lawsuit says. "This case concerns the Administration's sustained effort to do just that."

The lawsuit says the Federal Communication Commission - the government's media regulator - is being pressured to renew broadcast licences years early. It alleges the push stems from complaints from, and under the direction of, President Donald Trump.

FCC chairman Brendan Carr has said that the renewal requests were focused on "public interest", not retaliation.

The FCC reiterated Carr's message in an emailed response to the BBC on Tuesday, saying "all broadcasters have a legal obligation to operate in the public interest—even Disney".

"The FCC has been examining claims that Disney engaged in illegal DEI discrimination for over a year," the statement said. "The FCC will continue to follow the facts and law wherever they lead."

Disney and its eight owned-and-operated TV stations are plaintiffs in the lawsuit filed on Tuesday against FCC and its chairman.

Disney previously had been under investigation for its alleged diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) practices and for ABC's daytime talk show, The View.

But the notice for early renewal of licence from the FCC came a day after ABC's late-night host Jimmy Kimmel made a joke about first lady Melania Trump.

In the lawsuit, Disney calls the order by the FCC "unprecedented", saying that before then the commission had not called for early renewal in over 50 years.

"Acting through the Federal Communications Commission, the Administration has waged a retaliatory campaign against ABC for a single reason: it disapproves of what ABC broadcasts," the lawsuit says.

It cites Trump's own social media posts as evidence, including one in which Trump complained about ABC's coverage of him being "almost 100% negative".

In the same social media post, Trump also questioned whether their broadcast licences should "be terminated", and answered his own question: "I say, Yes!".

The FCC gave ABC and Disney 30 days to file applications, which, according to plaintiffs in the lawsuit, "ordinarily take months to prepare".

The lawsuit also notes that the FCC has never demanded early renewal applications from a group of stations commonly owned by a single broadcast network.

ABC and Disney have requested a "speedy hearing" from the court and a temporary restraining order.

Carr - who President Trump once hailed as a "warrior for free speech" - has long found himself at the centre of the administration's increasingly combative relationship with the media.

body.zh: 迪士尼和美国广播公司已提起诉讼，阻止特朗普政府启动早期许可证更新程序，称该网络因其社论内容而受到不公平的攻击。 诉讼称：“政府的审查制度非常不符合美国精神。” “本案涉及政府为此所做的持续努力。” 该诉讼称，联邦通信委员会（政府的媒体监管机构）面临压力，要求提前几年更新广播许可证。它声称这一推动源于唐纳德·特朗普总统的投诉并在他的指导下。 FCC 主席布伦丹·卡尔表示，续签请求的重点是“公共利益”，而不是报复。 美国联邦通信委员会在周二给英国广播公司的电子邮件回复中重申了卡尔的信息，称“所有广播公司都有法律义务为了公共利益而运营——即使是迪士尼”。 声明称：“联邦通信委员会一年多来一直在审查有关迪士尼参与非法 DEI 歧视的指控。” “无论事实和法律如何发展，联邦通信委员会都将继续遵循。” 迪士尼及其旗下八家拥有和经营的电视台是周二针对 FCC 及其主席提起的诉讼的原告。 迪士尼此前曾因其涉嫌多元化、公平和包容 (DEI) 做法以及美国广播公司 (ABC) 的日间脱口秀《The View》而受到调查。 但在美国广播公司 (ABC) 深夜主持人吉米·金梅尔 (Jimmy Kimmel) 拿第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普 (Melania Trump) 开玩笑后的第二天，美国联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 发出了提前更新许可证的通知。 在诉讼中，迪士尼称 FCC 的这项命令是“史无前例的”，并称在此之前该委员会已经 50 多年来没有要求提前续签。 诉讼称：“政府通过联邦通信委员会对 ABC 发起报复行动，原因只有一个：它不同意 ABC 的广播内容。” 它引用了特朗普自己的社交媒体帖子作为证据，其中特朗普抱怨美国广播公司对他的报道“几乎100%负面”。 在同一篇社交媒体帖子中，特朗普还质疑他们的广播许可证是否应该“终止”，并回答了他自己的问题：“我说，是的！”。 FCC 给了 ABC 和迪士尼 30 天的时间来提交申请，据诉讼中的原告称，“通常需要几个月的时间来准备”。 该诉讼还指出，联邦通信委员会从未要求同一广播网络共同拥有的一组电台提前提出续约申请。 美国广播公司和迪士尼已要求法院“迅速举行听证会”并发出临时限制令。 卡尔 - 特朗普总统曾被誉为“言论自由战士” - 长期以来发现自己处于政府与媒体日益对抗的关系的中心。 甚至在假设他的...

reflection.en: This news highlights the tension that can arise when those in authority are accused of using their power to silence dissent. Proverbs 28:15 reminds us of the danger when rulers act oppressively, emphasizing the importance of just and impartial governance for the well-being of all.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻突显了当掌权者被指控利用权力压制异议时可能出现的紧张关系。箴言28:15提醒我们，当统治者行事压迫时，其危险性，强调公正无私的治理对所有人的福祉至关重要。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Man in Chucky-style mask terrorises Philadelphia residents
title.zh: 戴玩偶面具男子在费城追逐并威胁居民，警方称

summary.en: Police in Philadelphia are investigating reports of a man wearing a doll mask who has been chasing and threatening residents, causing widespread unease in the community.
summary.zh: 费城警方正在调查一名戴着玩偶面具的男子追逐并威胁居民的报告，这在社区中引起了普遍的不安。

body.en:
A man in a creepy doll mask has been terrorising Philadelphia residents, running up to them and making threats, police said.

The Philadelphia Police Department said on Tuesday it is searching for the suspect, who allegedly threatened and chased at least half a dozen people near City Hall last week.

The man, who surveillance video captured wearing a scary doll mask, asked a woman if she was "ready to die", police told the BBC's US media partner CBS.

Police released photos and a video of the suspect, seeking the public's help to identify him.

In an incident on 12 August, the man was captured on surveillance video chasing a woman on a morning run around 5:30 local time (10:30 BST).

The masked man made threatening comments while holding his hand behind his back, causing her to stumble and injure herself, police said.

The man appears to be filming the incidents, holding a cellphone with its light on, Philadelphia Police Department Captain Jason Smith told CBS.

The suspect is facing charges including terroristic threats, simple assault and other offenses, according to the police captain.

Luanda Marinho told CBS she encountered the masked man while meeting a friend for a morning run.

"He starts asking, 'Do you guys want to race me? I bet I am faster than you. Want to race me?' He asked a few times, but none of us acknowledged him. Very weird," Marinho recounted.

They are considering changing their running route, she said. "It was just weird, like some twisted game."
body.zh: 警方称，一名戴着令人毛骨悚然的娃娃面具的男子一直在恐吓费城居民，他跑向他们并发出威胁。 费城警察局周二表示，正在寻找嫌疑人，据称该嫌疑人上周在市政厅附近威胁并追赶了至少六人。 警方告诉英国广播公司的美国媒体合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司，监控录像显示，这名男子戴着可怕的娃娃面具，询问一名女子是否“准备好去死”。 警方公布了嫌疑人的照片和视频，寻求公众帮助确认嫌疑人的身份。 在 8 月 12 日的一起事件中，监控录像拍到该男子在当地时间 5:30 左右（英国夏令时 10:30）晨跑时追赶一名女子。 警方称，这名蒙面男子将手放在背后发表了威胁性言论，导致她绊倒并受伤。 费城警察局局长杰森·史密斯告诉哥伦比亚广播公司，这名男子似乎正在拍摄这些事件，手里拿着一部开着灯的手机。 警察队长表示，嫌疑人面临的指控包括恐怖威胁、简单袭击和其他罪行。 罗安达·马里尼奥告诉哥伦比亚广播公司，她在与一位朋友晨跑时遇到了这名蒙面男子。 “他开始问，‘你们想和我赛跑吗？我打赌我比你们快。想和我赛跑吗？’他问了几次，我们都没人理他。非常奇怪，”马里尼奥回忆道。 她说，他们正在考虑改变跑步路线。 “这很奇怪，就像某种扭曲的游戏。”

reflection.en: In moments of unexpected threat and unsettling behavior, it's natural to feel fear and dismay. Yet, even when faced with strange and disturbing events, we can find solace in Yahweh's promise to be with us, strengthening and upholding us. His presence offers a steadfast anchor when the world feels like a "twisted game."
reflection.zh: 在面对意想不到的威胁和令人不安的行为时，感到恐惧和沮丧是人之常情。然而，即使面对奇怪而令人不安的事件，我们也能在雅伟的应许中找到慰藉，祂应许与我们同在，加添我们的力量并扶持我们。当世界感觉像一场“扭曲的游戏”时，祂的同在提供了一个坚定的锚。

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

title.en: US announces new sanctions on top ICC figures
title.zh: 美国宣布对国际刑事法院高级官员实施新制裁

summary.en: The Trump administration announced new sanctions against officials of the International Criminal Court (ICC), vowing to systematically dismantle the international body.
summary.zh: 特朗普政府宣布对国际刑事法院（ICC）高级官员实施新制裁，并誓言要“一砖一瓦地”拆除这个国际机构。

body.en:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has announced sanctions against the president and a senior lawyer of the International Criminal Court (ICC).

The move is the Trump administration's latest escalation in its campaign to "dismantle" the court which is empowered by more than 120 member countries to investigate war crimes.

Rubio said the US was sanctioning ICC President Tomoko Akane of Japan and ICC Senior Trial Lawyer Abdoulaye Seye of Senegal for engaging in the ICC's efforts to "prosecute officials whose government has not consented to ICC jurisdiction".

The ICC said it stands behind its staff and believes that measures such as those announced by Rubio "undermine the rule of law."

Rubio accused the court of being "a corrupt and fatally politicized supranational court that has maliciously abused its authority and exceeded its mandate. We will not tolerate its assault on state sovereignty."

The Trump administration has already announced sanctions on at least 11 ICC officials, including nine judges and the chief prosecutor.

The sanctions include asset freezes, travel bans, and restrictions on services from U.S. companies.

Those sanctions were issued in retaliation for ICC investigations into US personnel in Afghanistan and for warrants the court issued against top Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for alleged war crimes in Gaza.

Netanyahu has denied allegations of war crimes and accused the court of being motivated by antisemitism. Neither the US nor Israel are members of the ICC.

However, the state of Palestine became a member of the ICC in 2015, opening the way for the court's examination of crimes alleged to have been committed on Palestinian territory.

Trump's opposition to the court dates back to his first term in office, when he first described the ICC as a "threat" and told the UN General Assembly that it has "no jurisdiction, no legitimacy, and no authority" as far as the US is concerned.

Last month, Rubio called on the ICC's 125 member countries to withdraw from the court as part of a US government campaign to dismantle it "brick by brick".

Amid a growing pressure campaign, a US official said Washington would "watch with interest" who heeded its call and who did not.

The ICC, which was established in 2002, has ⁠international jurisdiction to prosecute genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes in member states or if a situation is referred by the UN Security Council.

"Measures targeting judges, prosecutors and staff who work towards the fulfilment of the mandate that was conferred to the ICC by States undermine the rule of law," the court said in its statement on Tuesday. "When judicial actors are threatened for applying the law, it is the international legal order itself that is placed at...
body.zh: 美国国务卿卢比奥宣布对总统和国际刑事法院（ICC）一名高级律师实施制裁。 此举是特朗普政府“解散”该法院的最新升级行动，该法院由 120 多个成员国授权调查战争罪行。 卢比奥表示，美国正在制裁日本国际刑事法院主席赤根智子和塞内加尔国际刑事法院高级出庭律师阿卜杜拉耶·塞耶，因为他们参与国际刑事法院“起诉政府不同意国际刑事法院管辖权的官员”的努力。 国际刑事法院表示支持其工作人员，并认为卢比奥宣布的措施“破坏了法治”。 卢比奥指责该法院是“一个腐败且致命政治化的超国家法院，恶意滥用职权并超越职权。我们不会容忍它对国家主权的侵犯。” 特朗普政府已宣布对至少 11 名国际刑事法院官员实施制裁，其中包括 9 名法官和首席检察官。 制裁包括资产冻结、旅行禁令和限制美国公司的服务。 这些制裁是为了报复国际刑事法院对驻阿富汗美国人员的调查以及法院对包括总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡在内的以色列高级官员因涉嫌在加沙犯下战争罪而发出的逮捕令。 内塔尼亚胡否认战争罪指控，并指责法院是出于反犹太主义动机。美国和以色列都不是国际刑事法院的成员。 特朗普对国际刑事法院的反对可以追溯到他的第一个任期，当时他首次将国际刑事法院描述为“威胁”，并告诉联合国大会，它对美国来说“没有管辖权、没有合法性、没有权威”。 上个月，卢比奥呼吁国际刑事法院的 125 个成员国退出该法院，作为美国政府“一砖一瓦”拆除该法院运动的一部分。 在不断加大的压力下，一名美国官员表示，华盛顿将“饶有兴趣地观察”谁听从了其号召，谁没有听从。 国际刑事法院成立于 2002 年，拥有国际管辖权，可起诉成员国内或联合国安理会提交的情况下的种族灭绝罪、反人类罪和战争罪。 人权组织对他们认为特朗普政府破坏国际法并扼杀世界各国政府打击有罪不罚现象的努力进行了反击。 人权观察组织国际司法主任利兹·埃文森在上周的新闻发布会上表示：“特朗普政府为其选择的任何人寻求一张免狱卡。” 埃文森发表此番言论之际，美国四个主要人权组织就特朗普政府的竞选活动起诉...

reflection.en: When institutions designed to uphold international justice are threatened, it can feel as though the very framework for accountability is being dismantled. Yahweh's word laments when the law is paralyzed and justice cannot prevail, reminding us of the profound human need for fair and impartial systems. Even amidst such challenges, the call to seek justice...
reflection.zh: 当旨在维护国际正义的机构受到威胁时，人们会感到问责的框架正在被拆解。雅伟的话语哀叹律法瘫痪、公义无法伸张的境况，提醒我们人类对公平公正体系的深切需求。即使面对这样的挑战，寻求公义和维护正直的呼召对雅伟的追随者来说依然不变。

verse.textEn: The law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails. The wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.
verse.textZh: 因此律法放松，公理也不显明；恶人围困义人，所以公理显然颠倒。

title.en: Judge swapped in Trump's defamation case against BBC
title.zh: 法官将特朗普诽谤案转判给BBC

summary.en: A judge who was recently nominated by the US president to serve in Florida's federal court will now preside over his $10bn defamation case against the BBC.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A judge who was recently nominated by Donald Trump to serve in Florida's federal court has taken over as judge in the US president's $10bn defamation case against the BBC.

Jeffrey Kuntz was nominated as a federal judge by Trump in April and confirmed by a 51-46 majority in the Republican-led Senate last month.

He was previously an appeals court judge in Florida and replaces Judge Roy Altman, who had also been nominated by Trump in 2019.

Altman was previously overseeing the case in which Trump is suing the BBC over the way its Panorama programme edited a speech he gave outside the Capitol in Washington DC on 6 January 2021.

It is one of 17 cases that have been transferred to Kuntz following his appointment to the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida in July.

Announcing the nomination in April on his social media platform, Truth Social, Trump praised Kuntz's work in Florida's Fourth District Court of Appeal, saying "Jeffrey has been TOUGH and SMART and delivered strong results for the Sunshine State."

Trump's case against the BBC is currently scheduled for a trial in February 2027. The president has requested a jury trial.

The broadcaster has previously apologised for editing together two different sections of the speech he gave before the 2021 Capitol riots.

But the BBC has asked for the case to be dismissed, arguing that the programme did not meet the legal criteria for defamation and that the Florida court does not have jurisdiction over the corporation because the programme was not available there.

As a Florida appeals judge, Kuntz was involved in another defamation case brought by the president.

On 12 February 2025, he was one of three judges who ruled in Trump's favour to allow the president to continue a lawsuit against the Pulitzer Prize board after it honoured the New York Times and Washington Post for reporting on purported Russian interference in the 2016 presidential election. The case is ongoing.

Kuntz's appointment in April by Trump prompted accusations of a conflict of interest from opponents as it emerged he had been in discussions about a potential federal court appointment at the time of the Pulitzer case.

Kuntz said Florida judicial ethics rules had not required him to step aside from the case, and he was only contacted by the White House after he had given his legal opinion.

As an appeals judge, Kuntz was also involved in a wide variety of other cases, ranging from the release of information from grand jury proceedings about late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, to whether a survivor of the 2016 Pulse nightclub shooting could sue a security company that trained and employed the shooter.
body.zh: 最近被唐纳德·特朗普提名在佛罗里达州联邦法院任职的一名法官已接任美国总统针对 BBC 的 100 亿美元诽谤案的法官。 杰弗里·昆茨 (Jeffrey Kuntz) 于 4 月被特朗普提名为联邦法官，并于上个月在共和党领导的参议院以 51 比 46 的多数票获得确认。 他此前曾担任佛罗里达州上诉法院法官，并接替同样于 2019 年被特朗普提名的罗伊·奥尔特曼法官。 奥尔特曼此前负责监督特朗普起诉 BBC 的案件，原因是其全景节目编辑了他于 2021 年 1 月 6 日在华盛顿特区国会大厦外发表的演讲。 这是昆茨 7 月被任命为美国佛罗里达州南区地方法院法官后移交给他的 17 起案件之一。 特朗普四月份在他的社交媒体平台Truth Social上宣布提名时，赞扬了昆茨在佛罗里达州第四地区上诉法院的工作，称“杰弗里既坚强又聪明，为阳光之州带来了强劲的成果。” 特朗普针对 BBC 的案件目前定于 2027 年 2 月进行审判。总统已要求陪审团审判。 该广播公司此前曾因将他在 2021 年国会大厦骚乱之前发表的演讲的两个不同部分剪辑在一起而道歉。 但英国广播公司 (BBC) 要求驳回此案，认为该计划不符合诽谤的法律标准，并且佛罗里达州法院对该公司没有管辖权，因为该计划在那里不可用。 作为佛罗里达州上诉法官，昆茨卷入了总统提起的另一起诽谤案。 2025 年 2 月 12 日，他是做出对特朗普有利的三名法官之一，允许总统继续对普利策奖委员会提起诉讼，此前普利策奖委员会表彰了《纽约时报》和《华盛顿邮报》报道所谓的俄罗斯干预 2016 年总统选举的行为。案件正在审理中。 特朗普四月份对昆茨的任命引发了反对者的利益冲突指控，因为有消息称，在普利策案发生时，他一直在讨论可能的联邦法院任命。 昆茨表示，佛罗里达州司法道德规则并未要求他回避此案，白宫只是在他给出法律意见后才与他联系。 作为一名上诉法官，昆茨还参与了各种其他案件，从大陪审团程序中有关已故性犯罪者杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的信息的发布，到 2016 年 Pulse 夜总会枪击事件的幸存者是否可以起诉培训和雇用枪手的保安公司。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Minors living alone on Ceuta's streets at risk of abuse
title.zh: 独居休达街头的未成年人面临虐待风险

summary.en: Several thousand unaccompanied minors have gathered in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa. Illness and abuse are rife, and the authorities admit they are overwhelmed.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Several thousand unaccompanied minors have gathered in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa. Illness and abuse are rife, and the authorities admit they are overwhelmed.

It's 8 a.m. at the Tarajal industrial park in the autonomous city of Ceuta. But there are no workers and truck drivers to be seen near the warehouses today. Instead, there are makeshift tents, some of them made out of cardboard, with mainly children and teenagers sleeping under dirty blankets.

According to certain estimates, there could be between 3,000 and 5,000 unaccompanied minors in Ceuta. Some are living on the streets because they cannot find a spot in one of the already overcrowded reception facilities in the enclave.

Amina (not her real name), a 14-year-old Moroccan girl, and her brother were among the 80,000 people who crossed the border into Spain from Morocco in late July. Though most of these have since left Ceuta , some 9,000 remain, according to the local authorities — and many are minors. "

What's worst is that we don't have toilets," said Amina. "We have to go somewhere in the bushes, but I don't dare go alone."

Close by is a Moroccan woman called Malika (also not her real name) who has spread out several blankets for herself and her four children. She told DW she was not making enough as a cleaning lady in Morocco , adding that she earned the equivalent of €7 ($8) per day.

"That's just not enough to provide for everyone," she said. "School will start again soon, and I don't have any money for books, nor even decent clothes for the children."

That's why she decided to take part in the mass crossing of the Spanish border last month when she read about it on social media. But now she doesn't know what to do.

"One child got sick. He had a high fever, but I couldn't get help anywhere," she said. In the end, she made compresses with water and vinegar to see if that would help.

But now she is particularly worried about her 12-and 14-year-old daughters, because the number of sexual assaults has risen sharply in the past week. Police are currently investigating at least 15 suspected cases of rape. The local authorities suspect the actual number of cases to be much higher.

body.zh: 数千名无人陪伴的未成年人聚集在非洲北海岸的西班牙飞地休达。疾病和虐待盛行，当局承认他们不知所措。 上午 8 点，位于休达自治市的塔拉哈尔工业园区。但今天仓库附近没有看到工人和卡车司机。相反，有临时帐篷，其中一些是用纸板制成的，主要是儿童和青少年睡在肮脏的毯子下。 据估计，休达可能有 3,000 至 5,000 名无人陪伴的未成年人。有些人流落街头，因为他们在飞地已经人满为患的接待设施中找不到一席之地。 阿米娜（化名）是一名 14 岁的摩洛哥女孩，她和她的兄弟是 7 月底从摩洛哥越过边境进入西班牙的 8 万人中的一员。据当地政府称，尽管其中大多数人已经离开休达，但仍有约 9,000 人留下，其中许多人是未成年人。 ” 最糟糕的是我们没有厕所，”阿米娜说。 “我们必须去灌木丛里的某个地方，但我不敢一个人去。” 附近是一位名叫马利卡（Malika）（也不是她的真名）的摩洛哥妇女，她为自己和四个孩子铺好了几条毯子。她告诉德国之声，她在摩洛哥做清洁工赚的钱不够多，并补充说她每天的收入相当于 7 欧元（8 美元）。 “这还不足以养活所有人，”她说。 “学校马上就要开学了，我没有钱买书，甚至没有钱给孩子们穿像样的衣服。” 这就是为什么她上个月在社交媒体上看到有关大规模穿越西班牙边境的报道后决定参加这一活动。但现在她不知道该怎么办。 “一个孩子生病了。他发高烧，但我无法在任何地方获得帮助，”她说。最后，她用水和醋做了敷布，看看是否有帮助。 但现在她特别担心自己12岁和14岁的女儿，因为过去一周性侵犯的数量急剧上升。警方目前正在调查至少15起疑似强奸案。地方当局怀疑实际病例数要高得多。 休达大学医院的急诊医生苏珊娜·阿斯卡索说，她最近几天治疗了几名年轻女孩。 “就在昨天，另一名 12 岁的孩子来到急诊室，”她说。 “她说其他移民骚扰了她，并对她进行了不恰当的触摸。她到达这里时非常害怕，流着泪。她和一名在街上发现她的妇女在一起。那个妇女救了这个女孩。” 阿斯卡索表示，对于“18 岁以下的女孩”来说，情况尤其困难，她们“尤其面临风险”。她补充说，存在着严重的不平衡……

title.en: Afghanistan: Only 5% of labor market are women under Taliban
title.zh: 阿富汗：塔利班统治下女性仅占劳动力市场的 5%

summary.en: The International Labour Organization estimates that only 5.1% of workers in Afghanistan are women, five years after the Taliban's return to power. That's less than a third of the proportion in 2019 and 2020.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 国际劳工组织估计，塔利班重新掌权五年后，阿富汗工人中只有 5.1% 是女性。这还不到 2019 年和 2020 年比例的三分之一。 根据国际劳工组织 (ILO) 周二发布的一份报告，自塔利班重新掌权以来的五年里，阿富汗劳动力市场中女性的比例已下降至每 20 人中就有 1 人左右。 国际劳工组织写道：“在妇女接受教育和就业的机会受到严格限制的背景下，阿富汗的女性劳动力参与率预计在全球第二低，到 2026 年仅为 5.1%。” 它呼吁采取紧急措施应对妇女的“严重排斥”，并表示这对于增强阿富汗经济的整体弹性至关重要。 随着美国和其他北约部队撤军，塔利班于 2021 年 8 月迅速重新掌权，结束了妇女在多年的伊斯兰强硬统治后享有相对改善的经济和教育自由的 20 年时期。 该联合国组织警告说，自 2021 年以来，劳动力市场将发生“重大的人口和制度变化”，其中许多变化使女性处于不利地位。 国际劳工组织阿富汗办事处主任兼高级协调员蒂特·哈比亚卡雷 (Tite Habiyakare) 表示：“在如此大比例的人口仍被排除在经济活动之外的情况下，阿富汗无法建立一个有弹性的劳动力市场。” 报告称，塔利班接管五年后，阿富汗劳动力市场仍“承受相当大的压力”，仅从 2021 年的崩溃中略有恢复。 当塔利班在新冠病毒大流行期间卷土重来以及西方军队和资金外流时，阿富汗的 GDP 下降了约 15%。 2022 年，该数字仍深陷负值区域，此后才勉强进入正增长区域，远未恢复到塔利班之前的水平。 从绝对值来看，就业人数已经开始上升，但速度还不够快，无法跟上人口增长的速度——无论是国内人口还是移民回国造成的——这意味着工作人口的比例正趋于平稳，仅占总人口的不到三分之一。 该文件还呼吁增加对代表性劳动力数据收集的投资，并警告说，其数据依赖于模型估计，而模型估计“存在相当大的不确定性，应谨慎解释”。 报告称，移民，特别是来自伊朗和巴基斯坦的移民的大规模回返，已成为“阿富汗面临的劳动力市场的决定性挑战之一”。 2023年至今年5月底，已有超过600万阿富汗人从伊朗和巴基斯坦返回...

title.en: Should India be worried about the Mecca defense pact?
title.zh: 印度是否应该担忧麦加防务协议？

summary.en: A new defense agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey is integrating Pakistan more deeply into the Middle East's security framework. This development raises questions about how India will react to the evolving geopolitical landscape.
summary.zh: 巴基斯坦、沙特阿拉伯和土耳其之间的一项新防务协议，使巴基斯坦更深入地融入中东的安全架构。这一发展引发了人们对印度将如何应对不断变化的地区局势的疑问。

body.en:
A defense agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey brings Islamabad deeper into the security architecture of the Middle East. How is India planning to respond?

The "Mecca Joint Defense Agreement" signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan on August 7, comes amid the Iran war and shifting security arrangements in the Middle East.

Saudi Arabia is seeking additional security partnerships as it faces uncertainty over the reliability of the US security umbrella. Turkey is seeking a larger regional role, while Pakistan is looking to turn its longstanding military relationship with Riyadh into wider strategic influence.

The agreement calls for collective defense, stating an armed attack on one member will be regarded as an attack on all three.

It also formalizes relationships that already exist . Pakistan has trained and assisted Saudi forces for decades, while its defense relationship with Turkey has expanded through military exchanges and cooperation.

For India , the question is whether the pact gives archrival Pakistan a deeper role in a region central to Indian interests.

Some Indian analysts see little immediate change in the regional balance. Others see a warning that India needs a stronger security presence in a region where its economic interests have grown considerably.

Saudi Arabia is a major energy and investment partner for New Delhi. The Gulf and the Red Sea are vital to India's trade and energy security.

The pact allows Pakistan to expand on its security role in the Gulf while providing an institutional framework for closer defense cooperation and potentially greater access to funding and technology.

However, former Indian High Commissioner to Pakistan Ajay Bisaria believes the agreement will have little effect on the basic dynamics of an India Pakistan confrontation.

"It does little to move the needle beyond the Saudi-Pakistan defense pact of last year, an arrangement that proved to have only signaling value for Iran, the US and Israel, at a moment when Riyadh was unsettled by the frailty of the American security umbrella," he added.

In the event of a future India-Pakistan crisis, the former ambassador said he does not expect the pact to fundamentally alter Saudi Arabia's position.

"For India, this is a pact to be monitored, not one to be unduly concerned about," Bisaria said.

"In the event of another terrorist attack from Pakistan, the situation is unlikely to look very different from Operation Sindoor, save, perhaps, for some added rhetoric," he said, referring to the name of India's response to a 2025 attack on tourists in Kashmir that New Delhi has blamed on Pakistan-backed militants . Islamabad has denied any involvement in the attack.

title.en: Fact check: How do I spot AI-generated images?
title.zh: 事实核查：如何识别人工智能生成的图像？

summary.en: Images created or manipulated with artificial intelligence tools are flooding social media. How can you know what's real and what's not? Here are a few tips.

body.zh: 用人工智能工具创建或操纵的图像正在社交媒体上泛滥。你怎么知道什么是真实的，什么不是？这里有一些提示。 任何拥有互联网连接和人工智能 (AI) 工具的人都可以在几秒钟内免费或花很少的钱创建逼真的图像，然后以极快的速度将它们传播到社交网络上。 用于创建人工智能生成图像的工具正在迅速改进，减少了明显的人工智能错误（通常称为人工智能幻觉）的数量，并使用户越来越难以确定病毒图像是否描绘了真实事件。 人工智能工具经常生成具有四个手指、过多牙齿或不自然身体比例的公众人物图像的日子已经一去不复返了。 另一个挑战是，虽然许多图像完全是人工智能生成的，但其他图像是使用人工智能部分修改的真实照片。 这里有一个例子：2026 年世界杯的真实转播图像，其中一名球迷被一个酷似阿道夫·希特勒的人取代。 那么如何识别人工智能生成的图像呢？ DW 事实核查提供了一些提示，可帮助您驾驭当今的信息格局。 您可能还记得 2025 年德国汉堡市一名叙利亚青少年帮助阻止持刀袭击的故事。 随着故事的传播，社交媒体上出现了对这一事件的相互矛盾的描述，以及人工智能生成的图像（如上图）。 该图像乍一看看起来很真实，但如果放大并仔细检查，您会发现明显的不一致。 这就是为什么花时间检查细节很重要。常见的人工智能错误可能隐藏在背景中，包括扭曲的对象和充满乱码的文本。 我们在 DW Fact check 中经常使用的工具是 Forensically，这是一个免费的在线照片取证平台，其中包括放大镜和其他用于仔细检查图像的功能。 还记得上面那个长得像希特勒的人吗？一个类似纳粹独裁者的支持者几乎肯定会立即引起广播公司、体育场官员和其他观众的注意。 然而，没有任何知名媒体报道过如此轰动的事件，体育场内也没有球迷分享从不同角度展示长相相似者的帖子。 这个例子强调了一个关键的验证技术：超越像素，问问自己事件本身是否有意义。 一种方法是检查值得信赖的新闻机构是否报道了明显的事件。 如果一张图像似乎显示了一个极不寻常或有争议的事件，但在可信的报道中没有证据表明这一点，那就应该发出危险信号。 你...

title.en: Designed to 'exploit' children: Meta faces a historic courtroom reckoning
title.zh: 旨在“剥削”儿童：Meta 面临历史性的法庭审判

summary.en: The trial's outcome could help reshape Facebook and Instagram, and leave Meta with billions of dollars to pay in penalties.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Meta knowingly hooked and exploited children, a United States federal court heard Wednesday in the trial of the social media giant on charges that it deliberately made Instagram and Facebook addictive to young users.

In what many experts have called social media's "big tobacco moment," a coalition of US states is demanding Meta pay $200 billion ($282.3B) in penalties for using technology specifically designed to foster addiction among children in a similar fashion to cigarettes.

Meta "exploited how kids' brains work," California prosecutor Megan O'Neill said in opening arguments, painting Meta's business model as one built to "hook the users, hold them for as long as they can, harvest their data, and then hide the truth from the public."

Meta's lawyer, Paul Schmidt, acknowledged that some users were harmed by the networks, but argued that the company had "tried to come up with tools to help them."

Before the trial began, the company denied all the allegations, insisting it had worked with parents, experts and law enforcement to incorporate protective safeguards for children.

This is not the first case seeking to hold tech companies — including Meta — accountable for these types of issues, but it could become one of the most consequential if it leads to sweeping changes on the platforms.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify, along with Instagram head Adam Mosseri.

Activists, including mothers of children they say were driven to suicide by their social media usage, rallied outside court.

One mother, Lori Schott, called out Zuckerberg and Mosseri, saying they "built one of those most powerful and richest companies in the world... But power does not excuse harm."

This is the first federal trial in what is expected to be a tidal wave of lawsuits also targeting TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube as families, educators and state governments charge them with harming the mental health of young people.

Meta, which has more than three billion users worldwide, is the sole defendant in this case.

In addition to financial penalties, the states are demanding changes to Meta's apps to protect young users, including limits to screen time.

title.en: Fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history leaves 2,300 dead in Congo

summary.en: The World Health Organization has said the current Ebola outbreak is on track to surpass the deadliest on record.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo’s fast-moving Ebola outbreak has now killed over 2,300 people and become the deadliest outbreak of the disease on record in the Central African nation.

The outbreak unfolding in one of DRC's most vulnerable regions is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever, with 4,945 cases including 2,325 deaths, according to government data.

It's the DRC's 17th outbreak, with a toll that has eclipsed that of the country's 2018-2020 outbreak when 2,299 deaths out of 3,481 cases were recorded.

The latest data shows 101 new cases and 33 deaths reported in the previous 24 hours. Over 1,000 people have recovered, while 730 remain in hospitals or isolation.

The outbreak has infected and killed more people at a greater speed than any other outbreak in history. The World Health Organization has said it is on track to surpass the 2014-16 Ebola outbreak in West Africa, the deadliest on record with more than 11,000 deaths.

Trish Newport, emergency coordinator with Doctors Without Borders, said the limited community engagement in the outbreak remains a key challenge.

"The community needs to be aware about the outbreak," she told The Associated Press news agency, adding that people "need to be involved in the response, and they need to know what the signs and symptoms are and what to do if they get sick. And this today is not happening in every single place where there are Ebola cases".

Starting from the first confirmed case, the outbreak reached 2,000 killed almost three times faster than in the 2014-16 outbreak.

Some families have lost up to 15 of their relatives in the epicentre, the Ituri province, Newport said.

"We rapidly need to scale up to be able to prevent more deaths from happening, more families and communities from being impacted," she added.

There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the rare Bundibugyo virus responsible for the current outbreak across six provinces in Congo's east. Trials for those are ongoing in Ituri.

Most new cases and deaths are being reported outside of the people being monitored. Challenges facing medical teams dealing with the outbreak also include strikes by some unpaid health workers, threats by rebel groups, anger from long-traumatised communities, bad roads making it difficult to reach all the affected territories, and misinformation claiming that Ebola isn’t real.

The WHO warned over the weekend that the outbreak is still moving at an "exceptional pace" ahead of efforts to track it, noting that it reached a weekly record of 579 cases and 304 deaths in the previous week.

title.en: Iran to go 'full offensive' if diplomacy fails as Trump threatens to bomb Oman
title.zh: 伊朗称若外交失败将“全面进攻”，此前特朗普威胁轰炸阿曼

summary.en: Iran has stated it will go on a "full offensive" if diplomatic efforts fail, following threats from the US to bomb Oman. Meanwhile, Iran has been negotiating an agreement with Oman regarding the management of the Strait of Hormuz.

body.en:
Iran will shift to a "fully offensive" military posture because efforts to negotiate a permanent end to its war with the United States have stalled, as the US ruled out extending a temporary ceasefire agreement.

Progress towards peace talks and a resumption of oil tanker traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz has ground to a halt, with no sign that the warring parties are moving towards ending the conflict that the US and Israel launched with attacks on Iran on 28 February.

"Iranian entities must be prepared to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and wider region, as Iran will be ready to make decisions and take action on difficult decisions," a senior Iranian official told Reuters news agency.

The official added that Iran would conduct a "timely and precise" military attack to break the US naval blockade if diplomacy failed.

Monday marked the day Iran and the US were expected to reach a final peace agreement under a memorandum of understanding signed in June aimed at ending the war.

Signed on 17 June, the MoU set a 60-day timeframe for the US and Iran to reach a broader deal on Iran's nuclear program and US sanctions.

The agreement, which declared the "immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts", quickly unravelled over a dispute about control of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flowed before the war.

Asked by reporters on Monday if the US was seeking to extend June's interim agreement, US President Donald Trump said no.

Iran said point 5 of the MoU gave it the right to manage the strait, which it shares with Oman, while the US rejected that interpretation. Hostilities resumed as Iran began firing on vessels it said were trying to sail through Hormuz on an unapproved route, and Trump said on 7 July that the pact was "over".

"Within the short period of a few weeks set by Iran, all the agreement's provisions must be implemented by the US. This is a precondition for further negotiations with the US," the Iranian official told Reuters, adding that mediators would share Iran's deadline with the US and regional countries.

Iran has been negotiating separately with its neighbour across the strait, Oman, to manage Hormuz, seen as a key component of a wider deal, and says it is close to an agreement, although progress has been slow.

Trump threatened to bomb Oman if it "gets in the way" of a US deal with Iran on the Strait of Hormuz and called for Iran to surrender.

summary.en: California is home to many billionaires. Soon, it will vote on a proposed wealth tax.

body.en:
In November, California will vote on a proposal to levy a one-off 5 per cent tax on the wealth of all billionaires in the state.

Google co-founder and billionaire Sergey Brin has already spent US$100 million on political donations to a group opposing the tax. Brin is hoping to avoid a potential tax bill of US$13 billion, a return of roughly 130-to-1 if that investment is successful.

Advocates of the billionaire tax claim it would raise US$100 billion in revenue, to be allocated directly to state-funded healthcare, food assistance and public education.

Supporters of the union-backed proposal also highlight that most billionaires currently pay lower marginal rates of tax than the average worker, and that the revenue is desperately needed to fill gaps in funding created by US President Donald Trump’s cuts to Medicaid.

Its critics, which include California’s Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom, argue the measure will drive billionaires and their tax revenue to leave the state.

Similar measures targeting the ultrawealthy are currently under consideration around the world.

In New York, Mayor Zohran Mamdani has proposed a 2 per cent income tax increase for those earning over US$1 million, and passed a property surcharge tax on second homes. Other US states — including Washington state, Maine and Minnesota — have passed or are considering similar income or wealth tax measures.

In the United Kingdom, a group of 120 millionaires have launched a “Proud to Pay” campaign asking the government to levy an additional 2% tax on wealth over £10 million.

Behind the public discussion of California’s billionaire tax lies a much deeper debate about spiralling global inequality.

Recent data from the US shows the share of economic output flowing to workers has dropped to a record low of 52.9 per cent in 2026. This means for every US$100 the economy produces, workers take home US$52.90 in pay, the smallest share since records began in 1947.

Conversely, the wealth of billionaires has accelerated rapidly. As of 2026, Forbes reports a global record 3,428 billionaires.

Perhaps most symptomatically, in June Elon Musk briefly became the world’s first trillionaire after the public launch of SpaceX. His wealth now sits at around US$800 billion.

Some blame globalisation for this explosion of inequality, but there are two other important related factors to consider as well.

title.en: China censors public mourning as it holds former premier's funeral
title.zh: 中国在举行前总理葬礼时审查公众哀悼活动

summary.en: While hailing Zhu’s legacy, authorities are wary that the nostalgia could lead to criticisms of Xi’s rule.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Flags at government sites are flying at half-mast and security vehicles are parked in the heart of Beijing, as China mourns former Premier Zhu Rongji.

Zhu died of an illness last week at 97 and was cremated at a funeral in Beijing on Tuesday. The ceremony, attended by senior leaders including President Xi Jinping, was kept low-key. No footage has been released.

Zhu, who served as China's premier from 1998 to 2003, is remembered as one of the country's most important economic reformers.

While hailing the late premier as a "loyal" party member, the Chinese state is also wary that public mourning for his era of reform can easily turn into veiled criticisms of the current government under Xi.

Xi was among the leaders who had visited Zhu in hospital or sent condolences after his death, Chinese state media reported on Tuesday. Others included incumbent premier Li Qiang and ex-president Hu Jintao.

After his death, state media described Zhu as an "outstanding member of the Chinese Communist Party" and a "time-tested and loyal Communist fighter".

He was cremated at Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery, an exclusive resting place for high-ranking officials and other prominent figures.

Meanwhile, online, posts about Zhu have been contained and censored - including an essay written by economist Zhao Jian, which remembered Zhu's era as a time when people were "properly poor" but saw a clear future ahead.

"There were no smartphones then, no short-form videos and no screens filled by the purveyors of anxiety," he wrote.

"The sky was blue, life moved slowly and people could say what they really thought."

The party has long been fearful of public reaction to deaths of senior officials and public figures.

The deaths of former premier Zhou Enlai in 1976 and former CCP general secretary Hu Yaobang in 1989 prompted widespread outpourings of grief that morphed into protests.

Zhu died just days before the Communist Party leadership gathered to commemorate the birth centenary of President Jiang Zemin, who died in 2022.

The death of Zhu and Jiang, two prominent leaders from the same era, has prompted a wave of nostalgia among many Chinese people for a time when the country looked as if it was going in a different direction - when it appeared that it may open to the world and allow more freedom for its people.

Previously purged under Mao Zedong's regime, Zhu was brought back into the fold after Mao's death in 1976.

Zhu served as premier alongside Jiang Zemin, who became Communist Party chief in 1989 and president in 1993.

The two men served alongside each other at the top of China's leadership from 1998 to 2003, leading China through an era of rapid economic growth and entry into global trade.

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼-中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan.

body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: After Hormuz, China looks to the promise – and peril – of the Arctic’s ‘ice silk road’
title.zh: 继霍尔木兹海峡之后，中国着眼于北极“冰上丝绸之路”的机遇与风险

summary.en: China has initiated the first regular shipping transits through the Arctic's northern sea route, aiming to establish an "ice silk road." This new maritime path, however, raises significant concerns regarding its potential environmental impact and geopolitical implications.
summary.zh: 中国已开通北极航线的首次定期运输，旨在建立一条“冰上丝绸之路”。然而，这条新的海上航线在环境影响和地缘政治方面引发了重大担忧。

body.en: China has established the first scheduled transit through the northern sea route, but questions remain over the environmental and political risks When Marco Rubio suggested that the world should look to new shipping lanes to bypass the logjammed strait of Hormuz, it’s unlikely he had the Arctic’s northern sea route in mind. And yet in recent months the promise of this 5,500km channel – cleaved through frozen seas by nuclear-powered icebreakers and illuminated by a sun that never dips below the Arctic horizon – has grown. Continue reading...
body.zh: 中国已经建立了第一条通过北方海路的定期过境航线，但环境和政治风险仍然存在问题。当马可·卢比奥建议世界应该寻求新的航道以绕过堵塞的霍尔木兹海峡时，他不太可能想到北极的北方海路。然而近几个月来，这条 5,500 公里长的航道 — — 由核动力破冰船劈开冰冻的海洋，并由永远不会低于北极地平线的太阳照亮 — — 的前景越来越大。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The pursuit of new trade routes like the Arctic's "ice silk road" highlights humanity's drive for progress and efficiency. Yet, as the story notes, such ventures also carry significant environmental and political risks that demand careful consideration. Yahweh's wisdom encourages us to foresee danger and take precautions, rather than rushing headlong into...
reflection.zh: 像北极“冰上丝绸之路”这样的新贸易路线的开辟，彰显了人类对进步和效率的追求。然而，正如报道所指出的，此类项目也伴随着重大的环境和政治风险，需要我们审慎考量。雅伟的智慧鼓励我们预见危险并采取预防措施，而不是为了短期利益而贸然陷入潜在的危机。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: A fake website and a deluge of CVs: the Australian firm embroiled in an FBI probe into alleged Chinese espionage
title.zh: 虚假网站与大量简历：澳大利亚公司卷入联邦调查局对涉嫌中国间谍活动的调查

summary.en: An Australian firm has been caught up in an FBI investigation into alleged Chinese espionage, involving a fake consultancy website that impersonated the Brisbane company. This fake site was among 13 websites seized by the US Department of Justice.
summary.zh: 一家澳大利亚公司卷入联邦调查局对涉嫌中国间谍活动的调查，其中涉及一个冒充这家布里斯班公司的虚假咨询网站。这个虚假网站是美国司法部查获的13个网站之一。

body.en: Exclusive: Fake consultancy impersonating Brisbane firm online is one of 13 websites seized by the US Department of Justice Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast When the first emails arrived, they were easily dismissed as spam. But as strangers continued to boast about their defence and security credentials, they became impossible to ignore. From mid-2025, a small Australian consultancy firm called Horizzen started receiving emails and strange calls from people applying for vague jobs in the United States. Continue reading...
body.zh: 独家：在线冒充布里斯班公司的虚假咨询公司是美国司法部查获的 13 个网站之一 关注我们的澳大利亚新闻直播博客以获取最新更新 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 当第一批电子邮件到达时，它们很容易被视为垃圾邮件而被忽略。但随着陌生人继续吹嘘他们的国防和安全资历，他们变得不可能被忽视。从 2025 年中期开始，一家名为 Horizzen 的澳大利亚小型咨询公司开始收到人们在美国申请模糊工作的电子邮件和奇怪的电话。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights how deception, even when elaborately crafted, often has a limited lifespan. While falsehoods may initially mislead, their true nature is eventually revealed, as seen in the seizure of these fake websites. Yahweh's word reminds us that truth ultimately prevails, and deceit cannot endure indefinitely.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻揭示了欺骗，即使精心策划，也往往寿命有限。虚假信息可能一时蒙蔽，但其真实面目终将被揭露，正如这些虚假网站被查获一样。雅伟的话语提醒我们，真理最终会得胜，谎言无法永远持续。

verse.textEn: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
verse.textZh: 口吐真言，永远坚立；舌说谎话，只存片时。

title.en: How to buy a ‘mega-dinghy’: the perilous new model of Channel crossing
title.zh: 如何购买“巨型橡皮艇”：危险的英吉利海峡偷渡新模式

summary.en: The Guardian China reports on the alarming trend of large dinghies, capable of carrying hundreds, being used for perilous Channel crossings. The article investigates the supply chain for these vessels, noting that large orders are readily fulfilled by manufacturers.
summary.zh: 《卫报》中国版报道称，载有数百人的大型充气艇被用于危险的英吉利海峡偷渡，这一趋势令人担忧。文章调查了这些大型船只的来源，指出制造商可以轻松满足大批量订单。

body.en: Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? Providing a large dinghy for use in the choppy seas of western Europe was not a problem, as long as the order was for more than 20 vessels, they said. The sales manager at the Chinese company even had an online brochure for an undercover Guardian reporter, posing as a prospective client, to peruse. They had a production capacity of 500 boats a month and, yes, it was possible to get even bigger ones for the right price. They could do a seven or even an eight-metre military-style dinghy for $1,678 (£1,238) a boat, without the engines, but that would be lacking CE certification, the mandatory mark that shows a product meets EU health and safety requirements. Additional reporting by Lyndon Li Continue reading...
body.zh: 载有数百人的船只是一个明显且令人震惊的趋势。但这么大的船只从哪里来呢？他们表示，只要订单超过 20 艘，提供一艘在西欧波涛汹涌的海域使用的大型小艇就不成问题。这家中国公司的销售经理甚至还为一位冒充潜在客户的卫报卧底记者准备了一份在线手册供其细读。他们的生产能力为每月 500 艘船，是的，有可能以合适的价格获得更大的船。他们可以以每艘 1,678 美元（1,238 英镑）的价格制造一艘七米甚至八米长的军用小艇，不带发动机，但这将缺乏 CE 认证，这是表明产品符合欧盟健康和安全要求的强制性标志。林登·李的补充报道继续阅读...

reflection.en: This report on the supply of vessels for perilous journeys reminds us of the vulnerable individuals seeking safety and new beginnings. Yahweh calls us to recognize His presence in those who are marginalized and in desperate need. Our compassion for 'the least of these' reflects our love for Him.
reflection.zh: 这篇关于用于危险旅程的船只供应的报道，提醒我们那些寻求安全和新生活的弱势个体。雅伟呼召我们要在那些被边缘化和极度需要的人身上认出祂的存在。我们对“这些最小的弟兄”的怜悯，反映了我们对祂的爱。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: The Fauci hearing was painful to watch. But we need answers on Covid-19’s origin| David Relman
title.zh: 福奇听证会令人痛苦，但我们需要新冠病毒起源的答案 | 大卫·雷尔曼

summary.en: Despite recent congressional hearings, understanding the origin of Covid-19 remains elusive, with a microbiologist observing a deterioration in public discourse surrounding the issue.
summary.zh: 尽管近期国会举行了听证会，但了解新冠病毒的起源仍然困难重重，一位微生物学家指出，围绕这一问题的公共讨论正在恶化。

body.en: Despite the recent hearings in Congress, we seem to be even further from the goal of understanding Covid-19’s origin’s than we have ever been As a microbiologist and infectious disease clinician, it has been tough to watch the recent devolution of public discourse on Covid-19 origins. It has been especially difficult for me to read the comments of Anthony Fauci about the origins debate in his now-public diary . And it has been painful to watch the televised spectacle hosted by the US senator Rand Paul on 29 July involving a hostile interrogation of Fauci. Despite many early pleas, including my own , for a dispassionate, objective assessment of what we know, don’t know and need to know about Covid-19 origins, we seem to be even further from this goal now than we have ever been – plagued by politicization, polarization and illogical thinking. David Relman is a professor of medicine and microbiology at Stanford University. He was an inaugural member of the US National Science Advisory Board for Biosecurity and president of the Infectious Diseases Society of America Continue reading...
body.zh: 尽管最近在国会举行了听证会，但我们似乎距离了解 Covid-19 起源的目标比以往任何时候都更远。作为一名微生物学家和传染病临床医生，很难看到最近公众关于 Covid-19 起源的讨论的转移。对我来说，阅读安东尼·福奇在他现已公开的日记中关于起源争论的评论尤其困难。 7 月 29 日美国参议员兰德·保罗主持的电视节目对福奇进行敌意审讯，令人感到痛苦。尽管包括我自己在内的许多人早期呼吁对我们所知道、不知道和需要了解的 Covid-19 起源进行冷静、客观的评估，但我们现在似乎比以往任何时候都离这个目标更远——受到政治化、两极分化和不合逻辑思维的困扰。大卫·雷尔曼是斯坦福大学医学和微生物学教授。他是美国国家生物安全科学咨询委员会的首任成员和美国传染病学会主席继续阅读...

reflection.en: The struggle to understand complex issues like the origin of Covid-19, especially amidst contentious public discourse, reminds us of the wisdom in seeking thorough examination. Proverbs 18:17 suggests that true understanding emerges only after hearing all sides and carefully scrutinizing every claim. This calls for patience and a commitment to truth beyond...
reflection.zh: 在围绕新冠病毒起源等复杂问题展开的激烈公共讨论中，我们努力寻求理解，这提醒我们彻底审查的重要性。箴言18:17指出，真正的理解只有在听取各方意见并仔细审查每项主张之后才能浮现。这要求我们超越初步印象，以耐心和对真理的承诺，从而走向更清晰的道路。

verse.textEn: In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right, until someone comes forward and cross-examines.
verse.textZh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理；但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

title.en: ‘TikTok wouldn’t open at all’: Taiwan simulates an internet blackout, with an eye on China threat
title.zh: “抖音完全打不开”：台湾模拟互联网中断，以应对中国威胁

summary.en: Taiwan conducted its first internet blackout simulation, prompted by concerns over the security of its undersea cables, which are vital for its digital connectivity. During the exercise in Taipei, air raid sirens sounded, mobile alerts pinged, and police directed people off the streets.
summary.zh: 台湾周四首次进行互联网中断模拟演习，原因是担心作为其“数字生命线”的海底电缆的安全。在台北的演习中，防空警报响起，手机警报提示音不断，警察引导人们离开街道。

body.en: Taiwan practised cutting off internet for the first time amid concerns about the safety of the undersea cables that form its ‘digital lifeline’ In Taipei, the streets swiftly empty as air raid sirens ring out and alerts ping on mobile phones. Police officers usher any stragglers into shelters, leaving the capital suddenly deserted. In cities across Taiwan, these kinds of drills are a fact of life every year , amid the growing threat posed by China across the strait, but this time there is something different. Continue reading...
body.zh: 由于担心构成其“数字生命线”的海底电缆的安全性，台湾周四首次练习切断互联网。在台北，随着空袭警报的响起和手机上的警报声，街道迅速空无一人。警察把掉队的人带进避难所，首都突然变得空无一人。在台湾各城市，随着海峡两岸中国构成的威胁日益加剧，此类演习每年都是家常便饭，但这次有所不同。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Taiwan's simulation of an internet blackout highlights the deep anxieties nations face regarding critical infrastructure and potential threats. In moments of such vulnerability and preparation, the ancient promise of Yahweh reminds us not to fear or be dismayed, for divine presence offers strength and help. This spiritual anchor can guide communities as...
reflection.zh: 台湾模拟互联网中断，凸显了各国在关键基础设施和潜在威胁面前的深层焦虑。在面对这种脆弱和准备的时刻，雅伟的古老应许提醒我们不要惧怕，也不要惊惶，因为神圣的同在提供力量和帮助。这个属灵的锚点可以指引社群应对复杂的挑战并建立韧性。

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

body.en: Bill passed Senate on Wednesday evening and is due back in lower house today. Follow today’s news live Follow our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast ‘Collapsing confidence’ in housing market, Wilson says Tim Wilson has jumped on that reporting around rent increases and says there has been a collapse in confidence since the budget which is hurting renters. We’ve had, since the budget, collapsing confidence, a lack of will to invest in housing that is going to be available for rentals. We’re seeing a complete disaster in the housing market, and we know that’s only going to do one thing while the government continues to overshoot its migration target, and that is an increase in rents on Australians struggling to save a first home deposit. There is an awful lot that goes into determining rents in Australia, and the thing that Treasury modelled in the context of the budget, what is the isolated effect of what the government actually changed about the housing market. And if I just step back for a second, we’ve got a broken housing system in our country, and it’s the renters of Australia who are bearing the brunt of really 40 years of government’s not doing enough about this problem. I think that Clare sadly needs to start taking a bit of responsibility for her housing policy. But also, Clare, stop gaslighting Australians, stop gaslighting the mum and dads who are currently watching this show and feeling the impact of your toxic housing taxes … She can sit on your show and defend her policies, but the evidence on the ground, the evidence from the experts, is that Labor’s toxic housing taxes are smashing the market. Continue reading...
body.zh: 法案于周三晚上在参议院获得通过，并将于今天返回众议院。威尔逊表示，蒂姆·威尔逊已经对有关租金上涨的报道进行了报道，并表示自预算案以来，信心已经崩溃，这对租房者造成了伤害。自预算案发布以来，我们的信心一直在崩溃，缺乏投资可供出租的住房的意愿。我们看到房地产市场发生了一场彻底的灾难，我们知道，当政府继续超额完成其移民目标时，这只会做一件事，那就是增加努力节省首套房押金的澳大利亚人的租金。确定澳大利亚的租金需要考虑很多因素，财政部在预算背景下建模的内容是政府对房地产市场的实际改变的孤立影响是什么。如果我退后一步，我们国家的住房体系支离破碎，而澳大利亚的租房者首当其冲，因为 40 年来政府在这个问题上没有采取足够的措施。我认为克莱尔不幸地需要开始为她的住房政策承担一些责任。而且，克莱尔，别再对澳大利亚人施以煤气灯，别再对那些正在观看这个节目并感受到你们有毒住房税影响的爸爸妈妈们了……她可以坐在你们的节目上，为她的政策辩护，但来自专家的证据表明，工党的有毒住房税正在摧毁市场。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to stewardship, provision, and the common good. 1 Peter 4:10 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with stewardship that serves neighbours, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到管家责任、供应与公共福祉。1 Peter 4:10提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以服事邻舍的好管家心态来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

summary.en: Want to get this in your inbox every weekday? Sign up for the Morning Mail here, and finish your day with our Afternoon Update newsletter Morning everyone. After a board meeting last night, the Sydney Swans AFL club says it will penalise players for a “serious breach” of...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Want to get this in your inbox every weekday? Sign up for the Morning Mail here , and finish your day with our Afternoon Update newsletter Morning everyone. After a board meeting last night, the Sydney Swans AFL club says it will penalise players for a “serious breach” of standards over an incident early on Monday morning. The government is expected to complete the passage of its controversial NDIS bill through the lower house today after making a deal in the Senate, and Erin Patterson begins her appeal against her mushroom murder convictions. Patterson appeal | Three judges will sit in Victoria’s highest court today to begin hearing an appeal by Erin Patterson over her conviction in the mushroom murders case. Swans dive | The Sydney Swans will sanction players for a “serious breach” of standards over an incident in Melbourne at the weekend linked to a report of sexual assault. The AFL’s chief executive, Andrew Dillon, said the allegations were “deeply concerning”. No arrests have been made and no charges have been laid. Bill victory | The government’s controversial NDIS bill will pass into law today after “substantial” amendments were agreed to in a deal between Labor and the Coalition, but some of the changes drew heavy criticism from the Greens, the ACT senator David Pocock and the disability community. Treatment fear | The federal government should fund treatment for thousands of women with breast cancer or endometriosis, and children with gender dysphoria, according to the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme’s advisory committee. Early draws | Pauline Hanson says people struggling to make ends meet should be allowed early access to their super savings. Our economics editor explores whether that would be a good idea. Continue reading...

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Aussies have long held a narrative of the resilient "battler". But recent history suggests the days of "she'll be right" may be behind us. Insight explores whether the little Aussie battler still exists or whether a culture of complaint has taken over. Watch Insight episode Wired to Whinge on SBS On Demand.

My successes in the art of complaining have ranged from a $400 payment from my bank when they failed to get me a replacement transaction card before an overseas trip, to a payout for medical bills from an airline on behalf of a friend's mother who was injured on the plane.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Born in the 50s, I grew up mostly in Sydney's inner-west in a time when even an eye roll was perhaps considered subversive of the notion that we shouldn't complain too much.

Because of this, I was always terrified of being seen as a whinger and would bury any grievances I had about all the ways women were treated.

Then feminists such as Germaine Greer and Betty Friedan hit my consciousness at around age 15, and I realised how much women endured, which made me have newfound respect for my mum.

Despite this awareness, I continued for the next decade to put up with many experiences I believed were just typical for young women.

I didn't complain when I spent half a day getting ready for a date, and they'd show up looking like they just fell out of bed; I didn't complain when my bum was pinched as a barmaid or when I'd have to lock myself in a storeroom to avoid the advances of a coworker.

It wasn't until my mid-20s, working as a social worker, mostly in the criminal justice system, that I was surrounded by many women who taught me I didn't need to put up with it.

Then, when I was a 34-year-old mother of two, I earned my law degree and really felt empowered to complain, as it taught me how to navigate the systems and rules that structure society.

I thought, "I know the system. I know how it's supposed to work, so I'm not going to keep my mouth shut anymore."

As a social worker and solicitor, who also worked for the NSW Ombudsman, I've learnt a lot from other “professional complainers” over the past four decades — even if some seemed worn from battling bureaucracy and institutions.

My "professional complaining" has largely been advocating for others for housing and those experiencing addiction. People call me up with an issue they need help with, and they know I'll gladly open my big mouth and advocate for them, wasting no time to get their issues resolved.

I think people could complain more, but they don't know how to do it successfully; there is a process you must follow to be a good complainer.

title.en: Want lower energy bills? You might want to skip this popular upgrade first
title.zh: 想要降低能源费用吗？您可能想先跳过这个流行的升级

summary.en: It's become a must-have on many home energy wishlists. But researchers argue there are smarter ways to maximise savings before taking the plunge.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Many Australians want to go fully electric. But it’s often hard to know where to start. Solar? A home battery? Or quitting gas?

To find the best way to make the shift, we modelled three pathways for a three-bedroom house in Melbourne’s western suburbs.

These pathways show it’s important to do things in the right order. It’s best to start by lowering energy demand through better insulation and stopping draughts, and then switch from gas heating to an efficient reverse-cycle air conditioner. Home batteries should ideally be done last.

We used benchmark data to model a household with ducted gas heating, gas hot water and cooktop, common electric household appliances and a petrol car.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Each year this household uses 5,300 kilowatt-hours of electricity, just under 50 gigajoules of gas, and about 1,230 litres of petrol (to drive 11,100 kilometres). This costs $2,477 for electricity, $1,494 for gas and $2,255 for petrol. Total energy costs are $6,226 a year.

We modelled replacing these with a 10-kilowatt ducted reverse-cycle air conditioner, a hot water heat pump and an induction cooktop.

We also modelled two further options: one where the household switches to a mid-range EV with a battery of about 60kWh and another where the household keeps its petrol car.

We tested three pathways to going electric. These don’t include rebates or the cost of the EV.

Here, the household adds a large 11.76kW solar array, gets off gas and replaces its petrol car with an EV.

Although total electricity use rises, the grid electricity bill falls due to solar. The new electricity bill would be about $1,800. Because gas and petrol costs fall to zero, the household saves about $4,400 yearly.

This pathway mirrors the first, but adds a 13.5kWh home battery at the end. The power bill falls to about $950. Savings would be about $5,300.

Here, the household doubles storage to 27kWh. The power bill drops to about $600. It doesn’t reach zero due to low solar over some periods and annual supply charges. Annual savings: about $5,900.

Governments offer a range of rebates and subsidies for households to go electric.

This includes $1,400 for solar, $1,400 for locally made hot water, and indicative discounts of about $2,500 to replace ducted gas with a 10kW reverse cycle air conditioner, $560 to switch from gas hot water to electric and $140 for induction cooktops. These are maximums, not entitlements, and there are eligibility requirements.

summary.en: Hundreds of lodged visa applications have been processed by fake or unregistered migration agents, according to a watchdog.

body.en:
Australia's migration agent watchdog has vowed to remove "fake agents" from the profession following multiple cases of unlawful immigration assistance.

The Office of the Migration Agents Registration Authority (OMARA) has sanctioned three registered migration agents in what the government described as an "ongoing crackdown".

Julian Hill, the assistant minister for citizenship, customs and multicultural affairs, said the government is strengthening immigration oversight.

"When people pay a migration agent they rightly expect a qualified person will do the work, not an untrained, unregistered fake agent," he said in a government statement on Tuesday.

"No one would put up with people borrowing registration numbers from doctors, lawyers or financial planners and neither should they when hiring a registered migration agent."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

OMARA's monitoring team was established in October and "proactively monitored" 85 registered migration agents during 2025-26, identifying 43 instances of non-compliance and addressing them through education, engagement and regulatory action, according to the government statement.

"Alongside the Investigations team, which examines allegations of serious misconduct, OMARA sanctioned 28 registered migration agents in 2025-26," it added.

In three separate cases, registered migration agents permitted unregistered individuals to provide migration assistance under the agents' Migration Agent Registration Numbers (MARNs), a practice commonly referred to as "front agent" activity.

In the first case, an agent’s registration was cancelled after OMARA determined that hundreds of visa applications submitted through three business ImmiAccounts involved either undisclosed immigration assistance or assistance provided by staff who were not registered migration agents.

ImmiAccount is the Department of Home Affairs' online portal for lodging and managing visa and citizenship applications.

In the second case, an agent was suspended after acknowledging that his son, who was not a registered migration agent, had provided immigration assistance on the business's behalf.

The investigation also uncovered allegations that clients had received falsified departmental correspondence intended to give the impression that visa applications had been lodged when they had not.

In the third matter, an agent was suspended after knowingly permitting another business director to lodge visa applications using the agent’s MARN while the director worked towards becoming a registered migration agent.

title.en: From 'I dont like it' to 'gayest party'? One Nation's complex history on LGBTQI+ rights
title.zh: 从“我不喜欢”到“同性恋派对”？一国党 LGBTQI+ 权利的复杂历史

summary.en: One Nation self-proclaimed status as one of Australia's 'gayest' parties has come under scrutiny.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Can a political party whose past and current members have described LGBTQI+ people as having a "mental illness" be one of the "gayest parties" in Australia?

It's a question provoked by recent comments from One Nation members in the past week.

When asked about former WA One Nation candidate Parminder Singh's comments — first reported by the ABC, that gay people have a "mental illness" — federal MP Barnaby Joyce rejected them as "highly offensive".

But some of Australia's most prominent LGBTIQ+ activists and equality campaigners say the party has more work to do in convincing the community it's truly living up to that title.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"It's probably fair to say the community’s reaction has been a mixture of confusion and incredulity," Equality Australia legal director Heather Corkhill told SBS News.

"It's not every day you have politicians from the same party declaring both that being gay is a mental illness and that they are the gayest party in Australia, all in the space of a week."

Singh — who has since apologised for his comments — isn't the only one to have said members of the LGBTIQ+ community have a "mental illness".

In comments first reported by The Guardian, One Nation WA senator Tyron Whitten said during a podcast interview segment about 'gender' in August last year that "there's male, there's female, and then there's mental illness".

"If you want to wear a dress, that's fine. I don't care. But ... they can't keep saying that, 'Hey kids, that's normal'," he added.

"You're going to be a boy or you're going to be a girl. And parents that are promoting this, I think that's child abuse."

Joyce is adamant the party is not a "pack of homophobes", describing that as a "vindictive trope" against One Nation.
